text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Observability gap detected for tenant HelioCorp in dedicated-pool "delta-3" (VPC). High error surface on /generate calls; traces missing, logs siloed. Paging on-call SRE.

ada: saw the bot. I'm taking this — ada (oncall). What's the impact? can customers see errors? any rollback triggers?

miguel: HelioCorp is reporting 5xxs from their production cluster. We see anomalies in metric ingestion for tenant_id=helio-42: p95 CPU/latency spikes but their traces are absent in our trace service. Logs are accessible for other tenants on the same host, so looks like a tenant-level silo.

kevin: tagging infra: this looks like the per-tenant forwarder for helio-42 failed to pick up log-shipping keys during the most recent rollout. There was a role change during the Dedicated rollout last night that might have left their forwarder without KMS decrypt perm.

ada: ok, immediate goal: restore log access and trace forwarding. Short term mitigation: attach temporary forwarder role and stream logs to S3 for debug. Miguel, can you confirm which instances host helio-42 workloads?

miguel: checking now. Instances: delta-3-gpu-7, delta-3-gpu-8. K8s pods: helio-prod-1..3 on node gpu-7. I'll run a quick kube exec to verify agent status.

kevin: if we need table access, I'll run IAM changes. We should prefer scoped, short-lived creds and audit entries.

ada: cs-helio, pls stand by to alert the customer we have a ticket and might need to enable debug logs (briefly will add noise). Don't promise ETA yet.

cs-helio: understood. I'll prepare a short message template and wait for the ok.

miguel: quick output from the node:
```
$ kubectl -n helio get pods
helio-prod-1 Running
helio-prod-2 Running
helio-prod-3 CrashLoopBackOff (forwarder)
$ kubectl -n helio logs helio-prod-3 -c forwarder
ERROR: failed to decrypt key: AccessDenied
```

ada: that lines up with Kevin's hypothesis. AccessDenied on decrypt means KMS key policy or instance role change. Kevin, can you validate the KMS policy for helio-forwarder-key?

kevin: validated. The policy accidentally removed role arn:aws:iam::redwood:role/forwarder-dedicated-delta-3. I'll re-add it with a 10m window. Applying now.

deploy-bot: Deploy started by kevin at 1955551810

kevin: applied policy delta. Requesting forwarder restart on helio-prod-3.

miguel: restarting pod now.

obs-forwarder-bot: Forwarder restart request accepted, rolling helio-prod-3 -> helio-prod-3b

miguel: restarted, logs show successful decrypts now. KVs are being uploaded. starting trace push.

ada: nice. can we confirm traces are actually populating the trace store? query the trace service for tenant=helio-42 and recent request id from CS.

miguel: querying...
```
$ curl -s "https://traces.redwood/api/v1/search?tenant=helio-42&limit=5" | jq .
[]
```

kevin: hmm still empty. Could be that trace-forwarder is buffering with a downstream Kafka partition mismatch for per-tenant topic. I remember a partition bump last week.

ada: who owns the trace pipeline? eng-ml or eng-infra?

kevin: infra owns the broker configs. miguel, can you check the forwarder logs for trace enqueue errors?

miguel: new log excerpt:
```
TRACE_PUSH ERROR: topic helio-42-traces: UnknownPartitionException for partition 14
```

ada: that's the gap. If the per-tenant topic partition got rebalanced without creating partition 14 for that tenant mapping, the forwarder will drop traces. Short-term plan: remap helio-42 to an existing partition or create the missing partition and fast-replay buffered traces.

kevin: creating partition now via kafka-tool. will create partition 14 and trigger a reassignment. ETA ~10m. I'll annotate with reason "tenant helio-42 missing partition after rolling upgrade".

ada: miguel, can you dump buffered traces from the pod (if any) to an S3 bucket so we can replay once partition is ready?

miguel: yes, dumping buffer -> s3://redwood-incident-dump/helio-42/195555

obs-forwarder-bot: Buffer upload complete (size: 18.4MB) -> s3://redwood-incident-dump/helio-42/195555/buffer.json

kevin: partition created and reassignment started. Monitoring replication.

deploy-bot: Reassignment job started at 1955552210

miguel: watching replication lag; leader moved to broker-3. no under-replicated partitions now.

ada: great. proceed with replay. Miguel, trigger the forwarder replay against helio-42-traces topic.

miguel: replay command:
```
$ ./forwarder replay --tenant helio-42 --s3 s3://redwood-incident-dump/helio-42/195555/buffer.json --topic helio-42-traces
```

obs-forwarder-bot: Replay accepted, pushing 12k spans

miguel: I see spans appearing in the trace store now. Querying again...

miguel: trace query result: 12 spans ingested, earliest timestamp 1955551700. We have trace continuity. :white_check_mark:

ada: confirm logs are now visible in the log viewer for helio-42 and that metrics p95 looks sane.

miguel: logs visible. Metrics: p95 latency dropped to baseline after trace replay correlates with a configuration flapping event at 1955551680. The per-tenant metrics ingestion had a short partition mapping issue, now corrected.

ada: good. next steps: 1) kevin to create an automated alert if topic partition for any tenant is missing or UnknownPartitionException occurs; 2) infra to add a canary verifying per-tenant topic mapping after rolling upgrades; 3) cs-helio to update customer with summary

kevin: filing infra ticket INFRA-4782 for automation + playbook. I'll add runbooks for making transient IAM changes safely. ETA for automation: 2 wks.

cs-helio: messaging HelioCorp: "We observed a transient observability routing issue affecting traces/logs for your tenant during a dedicated pool rollout. We've restored full visibility and are replaying buffered data. No data loss expected. Follow-up ticket incoming." Shall I send now?

ada: send now. include link to incident notes and s3 buffer for audit.

cs-helio: sent. HelioCorp acknowledges and appreciates the quick response. :pray:

ada: incident moving to monitoring. I'll do a handoff to night oncall in 30m with notes. Thank you all. Closing thread after 1h if stable.

oncall-bot: Incident 1955551234 status -> mitigated. If symptoms reoccur within 60m, reopen.
